notes.3i: This proved a difficult question as many candidates did not realise that the vector AB was the normal to the plane and point B was in the plane. Instead they usually opted for vector OB being the normal to the plane and the point A, or even vector AB, as the point in the plane. Even when the correct choice of the normal and the point were made there were often arithmetical errors in the numerical scalar product.
notes.3iii: Few candidates could give a correct vector representing the y-axis and many made errors in the evaluation of the scalar product of the vectors OA and OB. Answers: (i) 3x − 4y + 6z = 80; (ii) 30.8° or 0.538 radians.

notes.4iii: Few candidates were able to spot the relationship between the roots of f(x) = 0 and the equation in this section. Hence the necessity to choose the positive root of x = rarely occurred; however when it did those few candidates usually made the appropriate choice. Answers: (i) (x + 2)(4x + 3)(3x − 2); (ii) −0.369.
notes.5: Most candidates could use the laws of logarithms to evaluate e2ln3, etc. However, the idea of differentiating the expression, even though the gradient was clearly mentioned, did not occur to many. To make matters worse, those that did realise to follow this correct approach often did not notice that implicit differentiation was also needed. Answers: (ii) 5, 68.

notes.key_messages:
In order that candidates receive credit where possible for incorrect answers, they should remember to show
full working and reasoning. Incorrect answers without working cannot be given any credit, whereas partial
credit can be awarded if a correct method is shown. Where candidates are asked to ‘show’ or ‘prove’ a
result, marks will be lost if any essential steps in the argument are omitted.
